key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide-based coatings can be tuned for roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity by adjusting process parameters such as nozzle speed and spray distance.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process-parameter relationships and predictive equations that can help optimize coating production for desired surface performance.
method: Varied detonation spraying conditions for titanium-based metal-ceramic coatings
Measured surface roughness, coating thickness, and contact angle (hydrophobicity)
Fit parameter-property trends with inverse power and parabolic laws to identify optimal settings
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimentally observed relationships and newly derived equations linking spraying conditions to surface roughness, thickness, and contact angle.
watch_item: The reported optimization appears specific to the tested coating system and process window, so the equations may need revalidation before use on other materials or spray setups.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
